verified_signals.signal: Regulator statistical series 'Stevilo terminalov, ki jih zagotovijo rezidenti' (number of terminals provided by residents), table PTNS.PX, last updated 18/06/2026, gives the national estate: total ATMs 1,330 at 2026Q1, down from 1,346 (2025Q4), 1,374 (2024Q4) and 1,400 (2023Q4); ATMs accepting contactless transactions 993 at 2026Q1; POS terminals 46,659 at 2026Q1 (46,330 at 2025Q4, 47,235 at 2024Q4). That leaves 337 of 1,330 Slovenian ATMs (25.3%) not accepting contactless. CRITICAL DYNAMIC the earlier pass missed: the contactless count was FLAT at exactly 993 in both 2025Q4 and 2026Q1 while the total fleet fell by 16 - so the non-contactless tail shrank purely by DECOMMISSIONING machines, not by upgrading any. Separately, the series' 'ATMs with credit-transfer function' value drops implausibly from 917 to 100 between 2025Q4 and 2026Q1 and is a reporting artefact - do not rely on it.
verified_signals.source_name: Banka Slovenije PX statistical database - table PTNS.PX (terminals provided by residents)
verified_signals.implies: A hard, regulator-published addressable base of 337 non-contactless ATMs nationally. But the flat 993 shows Slovenian banks are currently retiring old ATMs rather than upgrading them - so the realistic play is replacement-cycle capture and estate-rationalisation/decommissioning services, not a contactless retrofit campaign. The shrinking ATM base against a flat-to-growing POS base confirms consolidation into fewer, richer (deposit/recycling) devices.

Retrieved values - A1 total ATMs: 1400 (2023Q4), 1374 (2024Q4), 1346 (2025Q4), 1330 (2026Q1); A13 contactless: 926, 955, 993, 993; A2 POS: 42552, 47235, 46330, 46659. verified_signals.entity: Addiko Bank AG / RBI / NLB d.d.
verified_signals.signal: [OUTCOME REVERSED SINCE THE RESEARCH PASS] The Addiko takeover contest resolved in RBI's favour, not NLB's. At the close of the acceptance period RBI announced (published 29/07/2026 17:30, reference 29/07/2026 17:00 CEST) that it 'has received declarations of acceptance relating to a total of 10,831,435 Addiko shares', corresponding to '56.16% of all Addiko shares subject to the Offer', and that its minimum acceptance threshold of more than 55% 'is exceeded'. RBI's threshold had been lowered to >55% on 09/07/2026. NLB's competing all-cash offer of EUR 37.00 per share cum dividend - threshold cut to 50% plus one share (9,750,001 shares) and the period extended to 29/07/2026 17:00 CET by Austrian Takeover Commission approval on 15/07/2026 - therefore could NOT reach its own threshold: acceptances locked to RBI after the 23/07/2026 17:00 revocation deadline left fewer than 9,750,001 shares available to NLB, and no shareholders switched from RBI to NLB before that deadline. RBI explicitly notes this 'does not yet constitute the publication of the official result' under Austrian takeover law, which was still pending at the time of verification.
verified_signals.source_name: RBI - Publications according to Austrian Takeover Law, interim status of acceptances as of 29/07/2026; NLB Group Addiko Takeover Offer page
verified_signals.implies: REVERSES the earlier read. Addiko's SEE network, including Addiko Bank d.d. Ljubljana, moves toward RBI group standards - it will NOT be folded into NLB's just-tendered ATM/CDS programme. Two consequences for Printec: (a) an RBI-led post-merger estate and platform harmonisation across Addiko's markets, procured against RBI group frameworks and central vendor lists; (b) RBI re-enters the Slovenian retail banking market, a structural change in the competitive map that NLB's Strategy 2030 assumptions did not price in.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - RBI threshold exceeded at close; official result publication still pending
verified_signals.followup: Pull the official Austrian takeover-law result publication and NLB's own withdrawal/failure announcement once issued; then size Addiko Bank d.d. Ljubljana's ATM and POS estate and map RBI's group ATM/POS vendor framework
verified_signals.verifier_note: The researcher's TERMS are all confirmed - EUR 37.00 cum dividend all cash, ATC approval 15/07/2026, threshold cut to 50% plus one share (9,750,001), period extended to 29/07/2026 17:00 CET, revocation window to 23/07/2026 17:00, merger clearance in Serbia/Austria/North Macedonia - verified against NLB's own Addiko Takeover Offer page. The RBI interim figure was exact: RBI's publication of 21/07/2026 states '10,703,509 Addiko shares... 55.50%' as of 20/07/2026 09:30 CEST, matching digit for digit. RBI's EUR 26.50 price is corroborated arithmetically - NLB's stated 39.6% premium against EUR 37.00 implies EUR 26.51. BUT THE CONCLUSION IS NOW WRONG AND I CORRECTED IT. verified_signals.signal: The Investor Day 2026 Payments deck lists 'Cash-at-POS rollout for improved convenience' as a named cash-transition initiative: 'Cash withdrawals move from branches to merchant tills - lowering cost-to-serve and improving customer service through longer hours and denser coverage, while keeping NLB central to cash flows.' Cash-at-POS means letting a customer withdraw cash from a shop till instead of an ATM. Separately, SEPA expansion completed to Skopje and Podgorica (NLB banks in SEPA went from 1 in 2023 to 4 in 2026, including NLB processing payments for the central bank of North Macedonia), with Serbia to follow in May 2026, and real-time remittances via Visa Direct and Mastercard MoneySend noted as 'Launch in progress'.
verified_signals.source_name: NLB Investor Day 2026 - Payments Transformation and Technology (PDF)
verified_signals.implies: Cash-at-POS requires terminal application changes, cash-limit and authorisation logic, and merchant cash-management across the acquiring estate - a POS software and services opportunity running in parallel with the ATM/CDS build. It also partly cannibalises ATM demand, so it should be read as a hedge on the ATM thesis rather than pure upside.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium-High - named initiative, no date or market sequence given
verified_signals.followup: Which markets get cash-at-POS first and on whose terminal software
